headline: Tribal Land Rights and Consent in Projects
fullText:
Ministry of Tribal Affairs

Tribal Land Rights and Consent in Projects

06 AUG 2026 12:34PM by PIB Delhi

The Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri. Durgadas Uikey informed in Lok Sabha on Wednesday that the Department of Land Resources (DoLR), Ministry of Rural Development is Nodal Ministry at the Centre for land related matters and has informed that Land and its management fall under the exclusive legislative and administrative jurisdiction of States as provided under the Constitution of India (Seventh Schedule- List II (State List)- Entry No. (18). Further, land acquisition and associated rehabilitation is undertaken by the Central and State Governments under various Central and State Acts.

Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change (MoEF&CC) has informed that proposals for use of forest land for non-forestry purposes are processed online through PARIVESH portal (https://parivesh.nic.in). Information relating to forest land proposed for diversion, category of proposal, details of the User Agency, current status of proposals, project afafected trees, etc. is available on the PARIVESH Portal.

Section 3(2) of the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 provides for minimal diversion of forest land for specific development facilities managed by the Government, subject to the condition that the extent of such diversion shall not exceed one hectare in each case and shall require the recommendation of the concerned Gram Sabha. The details to diversion of tribal land are not centrally maintained by Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA).

Further, Ministry of Panchayati Raj (MoPR), being administrative Ministry of implementation of Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 has informed that all matters relating to Panchayats, including land related matters of rural areas, fall within the purview of concerned State Governments and neither the State Governments have furnished details of such cases to MoPR nor does the MoPR maintain such details.

As informed by MoEF&CC, provisions of Rule No. 11 (7) of the Van (Sanrakshan evam Samvardhan) Rules, 2023 provides that the State Government or Union territory Administration can issue order for diversion, assignment of lease or de-reservation, as the case may be, only after receiving the ‘Final’ approval of the Central Government under sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Adhiniyam, and after fulfilment and compliance of the provisions of all other Acts and rules made thereunder, as applicable including ensuring settlement of rights under the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 (2 of 2007). Further, MoTA has been exhorting the State Governments and UT Administrations to ensure that no rightful beneficiary is deprived of their forest rights including compliance of Section 4 (5) of FRA which stipulates that the claimants cannot be evicted or removed from forest land under his occupation till the recognition and verification procedure is complete.

Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (R&R) of Project Affected Families, including its implementation and disbursement of compensation, is being dealt with by the respective State Government/Project Authority. Therefore, details of disputes relating to land acquisition, rehabilitation and implementation of Gram Sabha consent provisions in mining and other diversion projects is not centrally maintained by MoTA.

MoEF&CC has informed that the proposals for diversion of forest land received from the States/UTs are examined in accordance with the provisions of the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980, and the Rules and Guidelines made thereunder.

Grievances/ representations when received in the Ministry regarding violation of provisions of FRA are forwarded to the States/UTs concerned, for redressal of grievances, as implementation of the Act lies with the State/UTs. Further, State Governments have been advised to ensure that the interests of the Scheduled Tribes are properly safeguarded in accordance with constitutional provisions and various laws designed to provide safeguards to the STs.

Further, there are six pending legal matters related to diversion of tribal land in Scheduled Areas. The details are as under:

Three matters pertain to mining projects in the State of Orissa and are pending before the Hon'ble High Court of Orissa by way of Writ Petitions.

Two matters pertain to construction/widening of national highways through the State of Gujarat and are pending before the Hon'ble High Court of Gujarat at Ahmedabad by way of Writ Petitions.

One matter pertains to hydro-electric project in Chamba Division of the State of Himachal Pradesh and is pending by way of a Civil Suit before the Court of Hon'ble Senior Civil Judge, Chamba, Himachal Pradesh.

(Release ID: 2295352)
summaryText:
### OVERVIEW  
The Ministry of Tribal Affairs shared updates on tribal land rights and forest land diversion procedures, emphasizing state jurisdiction over land management and highlighting legal and administrative processes for project-related land acquisitions and forest land diversions.  

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS  
- Land and its management fall under state legislative and administrative jurisdiction per the Indian Constitution (Seventh Schedule, Entry No. 18).  
- Forest land diversion proposals are processed online via the PARIVESH portal (https://parivesh.nic.in), including details on proposals, user agencies, and status.  
- The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, restricts forest land diversion to one hectare per case, requiring Gram Sabha recommendation.  
- Diversions under the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980, require final Central Government approval under sub-section (1) of Section 2 of the Act.  
- Six pending legal cases related to tribal land diversion:  
  - Three mining projects in Orissa pending in the High Court of Orissa.  
  - Two highway projects in Gujarat pending in the High Court of Gujarat.  
  - One hydroelectric project in Himachal Pradesh pending in a Civil Court.  
- No central records of land acquisition disputes, Gram Sabha consents, or stakeholder grievances; implementation remains state-managed.  
- MoTA advises states to safeguard Scheduled Tribes’ rights per constitutional and legal frameworks.

“DBT in Implementation of Scholarship Schemes for Tribals”

The Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri. Durgadas Uikey informed in Lok Sabha on Wednesday that the Ministry is already leveraging the benefit of DBT Tribal Portal by accessing the data of beneficiaries submitted by the respective State/UT for monitoring and generating MIS reports for the implementation of pre-matric and post-matric scholarship schemes. The States/UTs have also been given facilities to upload queries, documents, utilization certificates, statement of expenditure etc. which has reduced processing time and reduced grievances.

The details of the number of beneficiaries reported by the States/UTs on the DBT Tribal Portal for the pre-matric and post-matric scholarship schemes during the last three financial years are given at Annexure-I.

The Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes are the Centrally Sponsored Schemes and implemented through respective States/UTs. The disbursement of scholarships is carried out by the concerned State/UT through their own portal or NSP portal. The progress made through the Portal are given as under: -

End-to-End Digitization: Transition from paper-based processing to scheme-specific digital portals.

Common Data Standard: Implementation of standard data format for seamless web-service API based data sharing between States/UT portals/ National Scholarship Portal (NSP) and the DBT Tribal Portal of the Ministry

Faster Communication and Online Processing: Online upload of Utilization Certificates (UCs), Statements of Expenditure (SoE), and queries by States, significantly reducing processing time and administrative delays.

Public Transparency & Outcome Dashboards: Integration of beneficiary and transaction data with the Performance Dashboard of the Ministry, DBT Mission, Prayas Dashboard, and NITI Aayog for outcome tracking.

The data of beneficiaries reported by the State/UTs in the DBT Tribal Portal have been useful for monitoring and generating MIS reports. Integration of National Scholarship Portal with States/UTs scholarship portal enables data validation and automated deduplication checks across schemes and databases.

Under Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes for ST students, to eliminate float at State level, minimize delays in release of scholarship, and ensure transparency of fund flow, the Ministry has adopted the SNA SPARSH Model for release of central share under Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme. This serves as a Just-in-Time Disbursement Framework under which the Central Share funds are release in "Just-in-time" as and when the bills are raised by respective State Govt for payment of scholarship. Once the bills for scholarship payment is approved, both Central Share as well as State Share fund is directly transferred from RBI account to Student beneficiary account on through DBT. This eliminates the parking of central share funds at state level and minimize delay in disbursement of scholarship.

Under Central Sector Schemes of Scholarship implemented directly by the Ministry, a robust digital mechanism is established through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP), Ministry’s Scholarship Portal and the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) to facilitate Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).

Removal of physical application process and manual verification by Institute/District/State authorities has streamlined approval workflows and reduced the overall application processing time. Transfer of Scholarship amount through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) into the beneficiary student bank accounts ensures that financial benefit reaches targeted ST students in time and without involvement of intermediaries.

Rehabilitation of Tribals affected by Ken-Betwa Link Project

06 AUG 2026 12:29PM by PIB Delhi

The Minister of State for Tribal Affairs Shri. Durgadas Uikey informed in Lok Sabha on Wednesday that Ken Betwa Link Project Authority under Department of Water Resources, River Development and Ganga Rejuvenation, Ministry of Jal Shakti has informed that Land Acquisition and Rehabilitation and Resettlement activities are being undertaken by the State Governments.

However, Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA) is member of Steering and Monitoring committees of Ken-Betwa Link Project, which inter alia monitors the progress of implementation of Action plan of R&R of Project Affected Families (PAFs). Further, MoTA had given a clearance for R&R plan for Scheduled Tribes Project Affected Families (ST-PAF) of Ken-Betwa Link Project, Phase –I, wherein the proposal provided by the National Water Development Agency, (NWDA) in 2016, mentioned that the Ken-Betwa Link Project, Phase-I involves displacement of a total of 1,913 Project Affected Families (PAFs) (population 8,339) out of which a total of 648 PAFs belong to Scheduled Tribes (ST).

MoTA has not received any complaint explicitly stating the issues of amounts recorded as disbursed but not having reached beneficiaries. However, Ministry of Tribal Affairs has received the various representations raising issues of displacement due to the Ken-Betwa River Link Project, which were examined and as the implementation of the FRA lies with the State Governments and UT Administration, these have been forwarded to the State Government of Madhya Pradesh and respective District Administrations for examination and necessary action.

As implementation of Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 (in short, FRA) lies with State Governments and UT Administrations, this data is not centrally maintained by MoTA.

Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) has informed that they have accorded the Stage-II approvals to two proposals pertaining to Ken- Betwa link project in Madhya Pradesh on 03.10.2023 and 06.05.2021 inter-alia stipulating the following conditions:

The State Government to ensure that the user agency implements the R&R Plan as per the R&R Policy of State Government in consonance with National R&R Policy, Government of India before the commencement of the project work. The said R&R Plan is monitored by the State Government / Regional Office of MoEF&CC along with indicators for monitoring and expected observable milestones;

The State Government to ensure that compliance of Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 has been completed in accordance with the relevant Rules and Guidelines issued by the MoEF&CC in this regard, before handing over of forest land to the user agency

Further, provisions of Rule No. 11 (7) of the Van (Sanrakshan evam Samvardhan) Rules, 2023 provides that the State Government or Union territory Administration can issue order for diversion, assignment of lease or de-reservation, as the case may be, only after receiving the ‘Final’ approval of the Central Government under sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Adhiniyam, and after fulfilment and compliance of the provisions of all other Acts and rules made thereunder, as applicable including ensuring settlement of rights under the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 (2 of 2007).

Moreover, MoTA has been exhorting the State Governments and UT Administrations to ensure that no rightful beneficiary is deprived of their forest rights including compliance of Section 4 (5) of FRA which stipulates that the claimants cannot be evicted or removed from forest land under his occupation till the recognition and verification procedure is complete.

The Rehabilitation and Resettlement (R&R) of Project Affected Families, including its implementation, disbursement of compensation, enhancing compensation and rehabilitation cut-off date, is being dealt with by the respective State Government/Project Authority.

headline: ELECTRIFICATION OF TRANSPORT AND OTHER SECTORS
fullText:
Ministry of Power

ELECTRIFICATION OF TRANSPORT AND OTHER SECTORS

06 AUG 2026 7:14PM by PIB Delhi

The Government is facilitating electrification and adoption of efficient electricity-based technologies in various end-use sectors through sector-specific programmes of the concerned Ministries/Departments. In the transport sector, the Ministry of Power has issued the Guidelines for Installation and Operation of Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure, 2024 and the Guidelines for Installation and Operation of Battery Swapping and Charging Stations, 2025 to facilitate development of Electric Vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure across the country. Electric mobility is also supported through the PM E-DRIVE Scheme of the Ministry of Heavy Industries and the PM-eBus Sewa Scheme of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

In the industrial sector, the Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) promotes energy efficiency and adoption of energy-efficient technologies and processes through programmes such as the Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT), Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) and Assistance in Deploying Energy Efficient Technologies in Industries & Establishments (ADEETIE) Scheme.

In the agriculture sector, electrification and solarisation of agricultural pumps are being promoted under the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM-KUSUM) of the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE). BEE also undertakes awareness and outreach activities to promote adoption of energy-efficient electric appliances and technologies, including e-cooking.

The Government is supporting States and Distribution Companies (DISCOMs) in strengthening and modernising distribution infrastructure under the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), along with capacity building and Demand Side Management (DSM) programmes.

For industries, particularly Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), the Ministry of Power launched the scheme titled “Assistance in Deploying Energy Efficient Technologies in Industries & Establishments (ADEETIE)” in July 2025 with an outlay of ₹1,000 crore, covering 60 clusters across 14 energy-intensive sectors. The Scheme facilitates Investment Grade Energy Audits (IGEA) and provides interest subvention of 5% for Micro and Small Enterprises and 3% for Medium Enterprises for implementation of energy-efficiency measures in their units.

For energy storage, Ministry of Power is administering a Viability Gap Funding (VGF) scheme for setting up 13.8 Gigawatt-hour (GWh) of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) with budgetary support of ₹3,760 crores. Further, a VGF scheme with financial support of ₹5,400 crores under Power System Development Fund (PSDF) has been approved for development of 30 GWh of BESS capacity for 15 States and NTPC Limited.

The Ministry of Power has not prescribed any sector-wise electrification targets. Electrification of end-use sectors is undertaken through policies and programmes of the concerned Ministries/Departments, while the Ministry of Power facilitates the transition by ensuring availability of reliable electricity, strengthening transmission and distribution infrastructure, promoting energy efficiency and providing enabling frameworks for emerging electricity-based technologies.

The Government has adopted various measures to enhance renewable energy integration, strengthen transmission capacity, and improve grid reliability to meet the growing demand for electricity. These measures include expansion of the Inter-State and intra-State transmission systems; development of Green Energy Corridors (GECs), deployment of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) and Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs); establishment of Renewable Energy Management Centres (REMCs) for forecasting and scheduling of renewable energy; implementation of ancillary services and the Real Time Market (RTM) for efficient grid balancing; and enabling flexible operation of thermal generating units to facilitate higher integration of renewable energy into the grid.

No separate target has been notified by the Government for increasing the share of electricity in the country’s total energy consumption. As per the India Energy Scenario Report, 2024-25 published by the BEE, electricity accounts for about 23% of the country’s total final energy consumption. The Government is facilitating greater electrification of suitable end-use applications, while simultaneously augmenting non-fossil fuel-based electricity generation and strengthening transmission, distribution and energy storage infrastructure to ensure affordability, reliability and energy security.

This information was given by The Minister of State in the Ministry of Power, Shri Shripad Naik, in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today.

IndiaAI Mission Organised AIKosh University Engagement Programme at Chitkara University to Strengthen India's AI Talent Ecosystem

IndiaAI Mission Deepens Academic Participation through AIKosh University Engagement Programme at Chitkara University

06 AUG 2026 7:00PM by PIB Delhi

The IndiaAI Mission, under the Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, organised the AIKosh University Engagement Programme (UEP) at Chitkara University, Rajpura, on August 6, 2026. The programme aimed to strengthen AI awareness, democratise access to AI resources, and equip students with the knowledge and tools required to participate in India's rapidly growing artificial intelligence ecosystem.

Approved by the Government of India in March 2024, the IndiaAI Mission is driving the country's vision of becoming a global leader in artificial intelligence by fostering innovation, enabling responsible AI development, strengthening indigenous AI capabilities, and ensuring that the benefits of AI reach every section of the society.

A key pillar of the Mission, AIKosh serves as India's unified data platform, providing access to high-quality datasets, AI models, toolkits, benchmarks and other critical resources that support research and AI application development. Through the AIKosh University Engagement Programme, the IndiaAI Mission seeks to introduce students and academic institutions to these national AI assets while encouraging hands-on learning and innovation.

As part of the programme, 250+ students from Chitkara University participated in expert sessions, live demonstrations and hands-on activities designed to familiarise them with AIKosh and the broader IndiaAI ecosystem. Participants also explored the AIKosh MCP (Model Context Protocol) and AIKosh SDK (Software Development Kit) which enables users to discover datasets and AI models using natural language, simplifying access to national AI resources and lowering barriers for both developers and non-developers.

Speaking on the initiative, Shri Md. Y. Safirulla K IAS, Director, IndiaAI Mission, said:

"Guided by the vision of our Honourable Prime Minister to democratize AI, we are committed to ensuring its transformative benefits reach every individual across the nation. This commitment rests upon three foundational pillars—People, Planet, and Progress—a philosophy prominently showcased during the IndiaAI Impact Summit in February 2026. As part of our University Engagement Programme, we will work to showcase the multifaceted elements of India's thriving AI ecosystem across educational institutions nationwide this year."

Welcoming the collaboration, Dr. Madhu Chitkara, President and Co-founder, Chitkara University, said:

"Artificial Intelligence is transforming the way we learn, innovate, and solve complex challenges. At Chitkara University, we have always believed in preparing our students for the technologies that will shape the future. Our collaboration with the IndiaAI Mission through the AIKosh University Engagement Programme reflects our commitment to nurturing future-ready professionals equipped with the knowledge, skills, and responsible understanding of AI. This initiative will empower our students to engage with cutting-edge AI resources and contribute meaningfully to India's vision of becoming a global AI leader."

As part of the next phase of the AIKosh University Engagement Programme, students will be encouraged to contribute datasets through the AIKosh open-source community and the University's institutional profile on AIKosh. They will also be encouraged to enrich existing datasets and develop proof-of-concept AI applications addressing public-good use cases. Outstanding student-led contributions may be considered for future recognition, creating a pathway from AI literacy and dataset exploration to innovation and real-world problem solving.

The AIKosh University Engagement Programme is a nationwide initiative designed to deepen AI adoption across higher educational institutions by introducing students, researchers and faculty members to India's national AI infrastructure. Today, AIKosh hosts 14,000+ Datasets, 300+ AI models and 30+ Toolkits, enabling researchers, startups, developers and students to build AI solutions using trusted national resources.

The programme at Chitkara University marks another step towards building a vibrant AI-ready talent pool and advancing the IndiaAI Mission's vision of creating an inclusive, responsible and innovation-driven AI ecosystem for the nation. Through the AIKosh University Engagement Programme, the Mission will continue to engage academic institutions across the country, fostering campus-level AI communities that contribute to datasets, models, applications, research and responsible AI adoption.

headline: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Effective use of water in AI Data centres
fullText:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

PARLIAMENT QUESTION: Effective use of water in AI Data centres

06 AUG 2026 6:59PM by PIB Delhi

Artificial Intelligence (AI) Data Centres do not, per se, require Environmental Clearance (EC) under the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Notification, 2006, as amended. However, AI Data Centres proposed as part of a “Building and Construction Project” under Item 8(a), i.e. built up area exceeding 20,000 sq. m or a “Township and Area Development Project” i.e. covering an area ≥ 50 ha and /or built up area ≥ 1,50,000 sq. m under Item 8(b) of the schedule to the EIA Notification, 2006 require prior EC. The EC for such a building project is granted by the State Environment Impact Assessment Authority (SEIAA) at the State/UT level.

During the appraisal of such building projects for grant of EC, various aspects such as availability of freshwater particularly in water-stressed regions, water balance report, generation of greywater, recycling and reuse of greywater are duly considered and appropriate environmental safeguards are prescribed. Further, the use and discharge of water and greywater during the construction and operation of AI Data Centres is regulated under the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, and the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981. Compliance with the provisions of these Acts, including the prescribed standards for water use and wastewater discharge, is monitored by the concerned State Pollution Control Board (SPCB) or Pollution Control Committee (PCC), as applicable.

Further, groundwater extraction for infrastructure/commercial projects is regulated in accordance with the guidelines issued by the Ministry of Jal Shakti vide Notification S.O. 3289(E) dated 24.09.2020, as amended vide Notification dated 29.03.2023.

The Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) has issued the District Cooling Guidelines, 2023, which, inter alia, recommend the use of treated water as cooling tower make-up water, wherever feasible, to reduce dependence on freshwater resources and promote sustainable water management. The Guidelines also emphasize the adoption of energy-efficient cooling technologies, optimization of cooling system performance, utilization of alternative water sources, and implementation of water conservation measures. These measures are particularly relevant for large cooling-intensive facilities, including data centres, and support enhanced energy efficiency, reduced water consumption, and sustainable operation of cooling infrastructure.

As per information provided by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, the ‘Resilience, Innovation & Efficiency’ Working Group of the India AI Impact Summit has been set up to examine energy efficiency, water management, and environmental resilience in digital and AI infrastructure.

This information was provided by MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE, SHRI KIRTI VARDHAN SINGH, in a written reply to a question in Rajya Sabha today.

headline: NAMO BHARAT REGIONAL RAPID TRANSIT SYSTEM
fullText:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs

NAMO BHARAT REGIONAL RAPID TRANSIT SYSTEM

06 AUG 2026 6:59PM by PIB Delhi

The 82.15 Km long India’s first Namo Bharat Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS) corridor namely, Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut RRTS corridor (which includes 23 km of Meerut metro network on same infrastructure) has become fully operational since February, 2026.

National Capital Region Transport Corporation Ltd. (NCRTC), the implementing agency for Namo Bharat RRTS, has informed that as on date, over 3.8 crores commuters have availed the Namo Bharat services since beginning of operation with a punctuality level of over 99%. Further, on Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut Namo Bharat RRTS corridor, effective multi-modal integration has been established with 03 Metro lines, 02 Railway stations and 04 Bus terminals, conforming to the guidelines outlined by Unified Traffic and Transportation Infrastructure (Planning and Engineering) Centre, DDA.

In Phase-I, three Namo Bharat RRTS corridors have been prioritized namely, (i) Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut, (ii) Delhi-Gurugram-Alwar and (iii) Delhi-Panipat. The Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut Namo Bharat RRTS corridor is fully operational since February, 2026. Further, NCRTC has submitted the Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) for the Namo Bharat RRTS corridors from Delhi to Karnal, Delhi to Bawal, Bawal to Behror and Ghaziabad to Noida International Airport. The Namo Bharat RRTS projects are cost intensive proposals and therefore, undergo intensive examination at different levels in Central Government. After such examination, Central Government considers financial assistance to RRTS projects, based on feasibility of the proposal and availability of resources.

NCRTC has informed that it has implemented several specific interventions across the Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut Namo Bharat RRTS corridor, such as, (i) TOD Zones of the Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut have been delineated and notified in Masterplans of Ghaziabad and Meerut along with special areas for TOD, (ii) Under Delhi TOD policy, 2021, NCRTC has prepared Influence Zone Plans (IZP) for the TOD Nodes at Jangpura and Sarai Kale Khan. Further, as per provisions of Delhi TOD Policy, 2026, any new RRTS corridor will automatically be considered under TOD in Delhi. NCRTC has further informed that a cumulative rooftop solar capacity of 7.8 MWp has been successfully installed to harness green energy. In respect of fare structure, NCRTC has informed that a 35% discount on base fare is being provided to all commuters. Additionally, NCRTC has also introduced concept of loyalty points, which are earned by commuters by traveling on RRTS network, which is used for availing discount.

This information was given by the Minister of State for Housing & Urban Affairs, Shri Tokhan Sahu in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today.

headline: Initiatives for transforming NER
fullText:
Ministry of Development of North-East Region

Initiatives for transforming NER

06 AUG 2026 6:35PM by PIB Delhi

The Act East Policy places the North Eastern Region (NER) at the centre of India’s engagement with Southeast Asia. A central focus of the Act East Policy is development of cross-border connectivity infrastructure. The India–Myanmar–Thailand Trilateral Highway and Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project are flagship projects under this framework.

The Act East Policy has also strengthened trade linkages between the Northeast and Southeast Asia through development of Integrated Check Posts (ICPs) and Border Haats.

The Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport project consists of Waterway component and road component.

The waterway component has been completed and inaugurated in May, 2023.

Road component consists of two lane highway (109 km long) from Paletwa (Myanmar) to Zorinpui, Mizoram.

The India-Myanmar-Thailand (IMT) Trilateral Highway has two parts:

Road construction in Tamu - Kalewa Highway has been completed and handed over to Govt. of Myanmar in 2009.

Construction of Kalewa-Yargi highway-section from km 112 to km 60 is complete and handed over to Government of Myanmar in October 2025.

A High-level Task force (HLTF) was constituted, in 2025, on the North East Economic Corridor (NEEC) with a mandate to assess the existing economic, infrastructure and investment ecosystem in NER; to identify critical gaps in physical connectivity, trade facilitation and sectoral investments; and to formulate strategies to attract public and private sector investments in NEEC projects. The report of the HLTF on NEEC was presented in the 73rd Plenary of North East Council in June, 2026.

The Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER) organized Rising Northeast Investors Summit in May, 2025 to catalyze trade and investment in NER. The focus sectors of the summit identified for attracting investment in NER were Tourism and Hospitality; Agro-Food Processing & allied sectors; Textiles, Handloom and Handicrafts; Healthcare; Education and Skill Development; IT/ITeS; Entertainment & Sports; Infrastructure and Logistics; and Energy. Collectively, the Summit and its pre-event roadshows garnered investment interests of ₹4.48 lakh crore through Memoranda of Understanding (MoU), letters of intent, and qualified leads from private investors, public sector undertakings, and major industrial conglomerates.

North Eastern Development Finance Corporation Ltd (NEDFi) plays a pivotal role in strengthening the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises sector and entrepreneurship developmentin NER by providing financial support for industrial, infrastructure, agri-allied projects, government schemes and institutional support. NEDFi also supports startup ecosystem of NER through North East Venture Fund.

headline: No concession or commitment on import of Ethanol for fuel blending from the United States
fullText:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry

No concession or commitment on import of Ethanol for fuel blending from the United States

06 AUG 2026 6:20PM by PIB Delhi

Recent claims in the media suggesting that India is importing and intends to import large quantities of ethanol from the United States (U.S.) for fuel blending are baseless and factually incorrect. As per the domestic policy framework, ethanol used for fuel blending under the Ethanol Blended with Petrol Programme is sourced entirely from domestic producers. There is no import of ethanol for fuel blending from the U.S.

Further, no concessions or commitments relating to the import of ethanol for fuel blending from the U.S. have been made in the India-U.S. Trade discussions. Accordingly, any suggestion of a policy change to permit large-scale imports of fuel ethanol from the U.S. is misleading. India’s fuel blending programme and ethanol procurement continues to be governed solely by India’s domestic policy requirements.

headline: Government Expands Digital Infrastructure and Citizen-Centric Services to Bridge the Digital Divide
fullText:
Ministry of Electronics & IT

Government Expands Digital Infrastructure and Citizen-Centric Services to Bridge the Digital Divide

2.21 Lakh Gram Panchayats Made Service Ready Under BharatNet; 5.01 Lakh Common Service Centres Deliver Digital Services Nationwide

06 AUG 2026 6:07PM by PIB Delhi

In line with Hon’ble Prime Minister's vision to democratise technology and empower citizens, the Government of India had launched the Digital India programme in July, 2015. At its core, the programme promotes three interconnected goals: strengthening digital infrastructure, delivering government services digitally, and empowering citizens through digital literacy and employment.

The Government is implementing the Digital India Programme through a whole-of-government approach to provide efficient, transparent and accessible digital services across the country. The Programme focuses on expanding digital infrastructure, broadband connectivity, digital inclusion and citizen-centric e-Governance services for all eligible citizens, including those in rural and remote areas. Details of some of the key initiatives are as follows:

Internet connectivity: Digital India has contributed to the rapid expansion of internet access, through initiatives such as BharatNet, which aims to provide high-speed internet to rural and remote areas. As a result, there has been a substantial increase in internet accessibility and usage across the country, and internet penetration in India has grown in the last decade.

● Telecom, Internet & Broadband Penetration: Total telephone connections in India grew from 93.3 crores in March 2014 to 133+ crores in March, 2026. In Tamil Nadu, the total number of telephone subscribers has crossed 8.41 crore.

● Internet subscribers jumped from 25.15 crore in March 2014 to 109.27 crore in March, 2026. In Tamil Nadu, the total number of internet subscribers has crossed 6.90 crore.

● BharatNet - Linking Villages to the Internet: As of June 2026, about 2.21 lakh Gram Panchayats (GPs) have been made service ready under BharatNet project in the country. There are 9,280 operational GPs in Tamil Nadu, including 210 GPs in Dharampuri.

● Under the Government-funded 4G Saturation Project and other mobile connectivity projects, till June 2026, 257 mobile towers have been commissioned in Tamil Nadu.

● As on 30.06.2026, 24,784 Towers are commissioned across the country under Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN) funded mobile scheme. The status in the state of Tamil Nadu including Dharmapuri District of Tamil Nadu is as under:

Towers planned | Villages planned | Towers on Air | Villages covered

Tamil Nadu | 356 | 445 | 257 | 308

Dharmapuri District | 14 | 22 | 11 | 19

● As on 30.06.2026, a total of Rs. 1886 crores have been disbursed under various ongoing projects of Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN) in Tamil Nadu.

Services delivery through Digital Public Infrastructure: Affordable data, assisted digital access points, and interoperable public platforms are enabling citizens to access welfare schemes, make digital payments, pursue online education, and participate in governance. Data costs have plummeted from Rs. 269 per GB in 2014 to roughly Rs. 8-10 per Giga Byte in 2025-26, making India one of the world's cheapest data markets.

● Aadhaar: Aadhaar created a trusted biometric identity platform for secure and instant digital authentication. Over 1.44+ billion Aadhaar numbers have been generated. In Tamil Nadu, over 8.18 crore Aadhaar have been generated.

● Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT): Through Aadhaar-linked DBT, cash benefits from various welfare schemes (318 Schemes of 56 Ministries) are directly transferred into beneficiaries' bank accounts. Over Rs. 52 lakh crore has been transferred through DBT nationwide.

● Unified Payments Interface (UPI): UPI has empowered millions of individuals and small businesses in rural and remote areas to make fast, secure and low-cost digital payments, significantly advancing financial inclusion.

o UPI serves more than 55.49 crore individuals, 6.5 crore merchants, and connects 731 banks on one platform, making it the world’s largest digital payment system.

o UPI powers 85% of India’s digital payments and nearly 50% of global real-time digital payments. State/UT-wise and District-wise UPI statistics are available at https://www.npci.org.in/product/ecosystem-statistics/upi.

● DigiLocker provides citizens with anytime access to authentic digital documents issued by original issuers. The platform has over 71.66 crore registered users, with more than 936.03 crore documents issued by 2,822 onboarded issuers. More than 2.18 crore Aadhaar enabled registrations have taken place in the state of Tamil Nadu to avail DigiLocker services.

● Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance (UMANG) provides citizens with a single mobile platform to access government services. The platform offers 2,575 services for individuals, including 17 services integrated by the Government of Tamil Nadu.

● e-Sanjeevani facilitates quick and easy access to doctors and medical specialists directly from your smartphone. The platform has served over 48 crore patients across the country including over 4 crore consultations in the state of Tamil Nadu.

● To promote linguistic inclusion in digital services, the Government has launched the National Language Translation Mission (NLTM) – BHASHINI, envisaged as a public digital platform for Indian language technologies. The Bhashini platform addresses communication barriers for India’s diverse population.

Assisted delivery of services through Common Service Centres (CSCs)

Common Services Centres – CSCs are offering government and business services in digital mode enhancing last-mile connectivity in rural areas through Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs). Over 800 services are being delivered through CSCs. As of May 2026, 5.01 lakh CSCs are functional across the country (in rural and urban areas), out of which 3.91 lakh CSCs are functional at the Gram Panchayat level (rural).

In the State of Tamil Nadu, 18,240 CSCs are currently functional, including 12,112 CSCs at the Gram Panchayat level. In Dharmapuri district, 498 CSCs are currently functional, including 412 CSCs at the Gram Panchayat level(rural).

Building Digital Skills: India’s digital transformation goes beyond mere access; it focuses on empowering people and institutions to use technology effectively, driving inclusive growth, strengthening digital governance, and enabling citizens across the nation. Major initiatives include:

Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyan (PMGDISHA) is one of the world’s largest digital literacy initiatives with over 6.39 Crore persons getting trained nationwide (against the target of 6 Crore). In the state of Tamil Nadu, 14+ lakh candidates were trained under the Scheme, including 64,813 candidates from Dharmapuri district. The scheme was concluded on 31.03.2024.

FutureSkills Prime, a collaborative initiative of the Government of India and NASSCOM, provides skilling, reskilling, and upskilling in emerging technologies. So far, over 34 lakh candidates have registered on the portal, with more than 23 lakh enrolled/trained in various courses, including over 5.81 lakh candidates from Tamil Nadu.

National Institute of Electronics and Information Technology (NIELIT) provides digital literacy and skill development courses, including ACC and CCC, through 56 Centres and a network of over 9,000 partner institutes across the country. 31.92 Lakh+ candidates have been trained by NIELIT during the last three financial years. NIELIT has a strong presence in Tamil Nadu through its Centre at Chennai, and 35+ partner institutes across the State. In the last 03 years, NIELIT has trained/skilled 37500+ candidates in the State of Tamil Nadu.

NIELIT Digital University (NDU) Platform: The platform delivers online and blended skill-based industry-aligned courses in emerging technologies, such as Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity etc. So far 2.75 lakh+ candidates have registered under the NIELIT Digital University Platform.

In addition to the above, various Government services, including issuance of certificates, pension-related services, and welfare schemes, are delivered through State Government portals and mobile applications. The Tamil Nadu e-Governance Agency (TNeGA) has developed the e-Sevai portal, which enables end-to-end online delivery of a wide range of citizen-centric Government services without manual intervention. The digital services can be accessed at https://www.tnesevai.tn.gov.in/.

Budget Allocation and Utilisation: The Digital India Programme is an umbrella programme comprising projects implemented by various Central Ministries/Departments and States/UTs, each with its own budgetary provisions. MeitY implements eight Central Sector sub-schemes under the Programme, for which no State/UT-wise budget allocation is made.

This information was submitted by Union Minister of State for Electronics and Information Technology Shri Jitin Prasada in Lok Sabha on 05.08.2026.

### OVERVIEW
The Government of India, through the Digital India programme launched in July 2015, has expanded digital infrastructure, broadband connectivity, and citizen-centric e-Governance services nationwide. The programme operates on a whole-of-government approach to strengthen digital inclusion, deliver government services digitally, and empower citizens through digital literacy and employment.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
- **Digital India Programme Launch:** July 2015, aligned with the vision to democratise technology and empower citizens, focusing on three goals: digital infrastructure, digital service delivery, and digital literacy/employment.
- **BharatNet:** 2.21 lakh Gram Panchayats (GPs) made service ready as of June 2026; 9,280 operational GPs in Tamil Nadu, including 210 in Dharampuri.
- **Telecom & Internet Penetration:**
  - Total telephone connections grew from 93.3 crore (March 2014) to 133+ crore (March 2026); Tamil Nadu: 8.41 crore subscribers.
  - Internet subscribers grew from 25.15 crore (March 2014) to 109.27 crore (March 2026); Tamil Nadu: 6.90 crore subscribers.
- **Mobile Connectivity:** 257 mobile towers commissioned in Tamil Nadu under the Government-funded 4G Saturation Project (as of June 2026).
- **Digital Bharat Nidhi (DBN) Mobile Scheme:** 24,784 towers commissioned nationwide as of 30.06.2026. Tamil Nadu: 356 towers planned, 445 villages planned, 257 towers on air, 308 villages covered. Dharmapuri District: 14 towers planned, 22 villages planned, 11 towers on air, 19 villages covered. Rs. 1,886 crore disbursed under DBN projects in Tamil Nadu.
- **Data Costs:** Reduced from Rs. 269 per GB (2014) to approximately Rs. 8–10 per GB (2025–26), making India one of the world's cheapest data markets.
- **Aadhaar:** Over 144 crore Aadhaar numbers generated nationwide; over 8.18 crore in Tamil Nadu.
- **Direct Benefit Transfers (DBT):** 318 schemes across 56 Ministries linked to Aadhaar; over Rs. 52 lakh crore transferred nationwide.
- **Unified Payments Interface (UPI):** Serves 55.49 crore individuals, 6.5 crore merchants, and 731 banks; powers 85% of India's digital payments and nearly 50% of global real-time digital payments.
- **DigiLocker:** 71.66 crore registered users, 936.03 crore documents issued by 2,822 onboarded issuers; over 2.18 crore Aadhaar-enabled registrations in Tamil Nadu.
- **UMANG:** Offers 2,575 services for individuals, including 17 services integrated by the Government of Tamil Nadu.
- **e-Sanjeevani:** Over 48 crore patients served nationwide, including over 4 crore consultations in Tamil Nadu.
- **Bhashini (NLTM):** National Language Translation Mission platform for Indian language technologies to address communication barriers.
- **Common Service Centres (CSCs):** 5.01 lakh functional nationwide as of May 2026 (3.91 lakh at GP level). Tamil Nadu: 18,240 CSCs (12,112 at GP level). Dharmapuri: 498 CSCs (412 at GP level). Over 800 services delivered through CSCs.
