headline: RAINWATER HARVESTING AND WATER CONSERVATION
fullText:
Ministry of Jal Shakti

RAINWATER HARVESTING AND WATER CONSERVATION

06 AUG 2026 4:49PM by PIB Delhi

‘Water’ being a State subject, the aspects related to water resources including its conservation are studied, planned, funded and executed by the State Governments themselves as per their own resources and priorities. The Central Government supplements the measures and efforts being taken up by the State Governments.

“Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari” (JSJB) initiative was launched in Surat, Gujarat on 6 September 2024. In June 2025, JSJB 2.0 was launched. The implementation cycle for JSJB 2.0 commenced on 1 June 2025 and concluded on 31 May 2026.

Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Catch the Rain (JSJB: CTR) – 2026 was launched on 1st June 2026 enhancing the scope of the Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari (JSJB) initiative and simultaneously integrating it with the Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain (JSA: CTR) campaign. The JSJB initiative focuses on intensifying community action and mobilization to build low-cost rainwater harvesting structures in low cost and saturation mode. The details of JSJB 1.0, JSJB 2.0 and JSJB: CTR 2026 initiatives are attached at Annexure-I.

The initiative leverages community funds, individual donations, Corporate Social Responsibility Funds and others for construction of low-cost structures like borewells, recharge shafts, recharge pits, using locally available material, to harvest rainwater, to boost ground water level and provide local tailor-made solution to water issues. The initiative also emphasizes convergent financing from various schemes of the Central, State and local bodies like Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G), Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation (AMRUT), Per Drop More Crop, Repair, Renovation and Restoration Components under the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana (PMKSY), Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA) and Finance Commission grants.

The objective is to ensure that every drop of water is conserved through collective efforts, following a whole-of-society and whole-of-government approach. By fostering community ownership, the initiative seeks to develop cost-effective, local solutions at the micro level for water conservation and ground water recharge. The initiative is guided by the 3Cs principle—Community, CSR and Cost, ensuring effective convergence and maximized outcomes. The Government promotes the initiative in partnership with State Governments and local authorities to ensure its widespread reach and awareness. The initiative aims at forging partnership with stakeholders such as NGOs, Trusts, Civil Societies and educational institutions to engage the broader community effectively. The progress of the campaign is monitored through online portal - JSJB: CTR (https://jsjb.mowr.gov.in).

In 2019, the Ministry of Jal Shakti launched Jal Shakti Abhiyan (JSA) as a time-bound, mission-mode water conservation campaign in 256 water stressed districts of the country. The Hon'ble PM of India launched the campaign in 2021 as Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain (JSA: CTR) with the message, "Catch the Rain: Where It Falls, When It Falls." Since then, JSA: CTR evolved into a national movement, reinforcing India's collective commitment to water security through localised action and institutional convergence. The JSA: CTR campaign was implemented nationwide and each edition had included a targeted focus since 2023 to maximize impact. The JSA: CTR 2023, with the theme “Source Sustainability for Drinking Water,” prioritized 150 special focus districts identified by the Jal Jeevan Mission. The JSA: CTR 2024 campaign, themed “Nari Shakti se Jal Shakti,” was carried out across the country with a special focus on 151 districts identified by the Central Ground Water Board (CGWB). The JSA: CTR 2025 was launched with the theme “Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Jan Jagrukta Ki Or” emphasizing deeper grassroots engagement, inter-sectoral convergence and innovative financing mechanisms with special focus on 148 districts identified by CGWB.

Government of India launched “Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY)” to enhance physical access of water on farm and expand cultivable area under assured irrigation, improve on farm water use efficiency, introduce sustainable water conservation practices. Har Khet Ko Pani (HKKP) is one of the components of PMKSY. Under this component, the scheme of Surface Minor Irrigation (SMI) and Repair, Renovation and Restoration (RRR) of Water Bodies schemes were included. The Ministry of Jal Shakti provides Central Assistance (CA) to States for the creation and restoration of Irrigation Potential (IP) under the SMI and RRR of Water Bodies schemes. The details of State wise CA release and Irrigation Potential created/restored for SMI and RRR of WBs under PMKSY-HKKP as on 31.07.2026 is given in Annexure-II.

As reported by the Department of Rural Development, the details of the total expenditure incurred on water-related works under MGNREGS during the last three years and the current year, for all States and Union Territories, are given in the Annexure-III.

National Water Policy (2012), formulated by Department of Water Resources, River Development & Ganga Rejuvenation, inter-alia advocates rainwater harvesting and conservation of water and highlights the need for augmenting the availability of water through direct use of rainfall.

The Government has prescribed various regulatory and enabling provisions to promote and institutionalize rainwater harvesting in buildings and development projects across the country, including:

Ministry of Jal Shakti notified guidelines dated 24.09.2020 and amendments dated 29.03.2023 thereto for regulation of groundwater extraction by industries, infrastructure and mining projects.

The Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) published the Model Building Bye-Laws, 2016, which recommend rainwater harvesting provisions for all types of buildings with a plot size of 100 sq. m. or more, mandating such buildings to include a comprehensive proposal for rainwater harvesting at the time of submission of building plans for approval, irrespective of the intended use of the building.

Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) has completed the National Aquifer Mapping and Management Programme (NAQUIM) for the entire mappable area of about 25 lakh sq. km in the country, including water-stressed regions. CGWB has also prepared the Master Plan for Artificial Recharge to Groundwater-2020 in consultation with the States/UTs. It is a macro-level plan indicating suitable rainwater harvesting and artificial recharge structures for different terrain and hydrogeological conditions, including water-stressed regions.

CGWB, in coordination with the State/UT Governments, periodically carries out the Dynamic Ground Water Resources Assessment to estimate groundwater recharge, extractable groundwater resources, groundwater extraction and the stage of groundwater extraction, and to assess changes therein over time. As per the assessment results, the total annual groundwater recharge in the country increased from about 432 BCM in 2017 to 448.52 BCM in 2025. During the same period, the proportion of assessment units categorised as ‘Safe’ increased from 62.6% to 73.14%, while that of ‘Over-exploited’ assessment units declined from 17.2% to 10.8%, indicating an overall improvement in the groundwater scenario. The assessment further indicates that recharge from tanks, ponds and other water-conservation structures increased by 12.93 BCM, from 13.98 BCM in 2017 to 26.91 BCM in 2025. This reflects an increase in the contribution of such structures to groundwater recharge during the period.

### OVERVIEW
The Ministry of Jal Shakti has launched the "Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Catch the Rain (JSJB: CTR) – 2026" initiative on 1 June 2026. The initiative enhances the scope of the existing JSJB initiative and integrates it with the Jal Shakti Abhiyan: Catch the Rain (JSA: CTR) campaign to intensify community-led rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge nationwide.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
* **JSJB Initiative Timeline:** The JSJB initiative was launched in Surat, Gujarat on 6 September 2024; JSJB 2.0 was launched in June 2025 (implementation cycle: 1 June 2025 to 31 May 2026); JSJB: CTR 2026 was launched on 1 June 2026.
* **JSJB Focus and Financing:** The initiative focuses on intensifying community action to build low-cost rainwater harvesting structures (e.g., borewells, recharge shafts, recharge pits) using locally available materials. It leverages community funds, individual donations, and Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funds, and emphasizes convergent financing from schemes such as VB-G RAM G, AMRUT, Per Drop More Crop, PMKSY-HKKP (SMI and RRR of Water Bodies), CAMPA, and Finance Commission grants.
* **JSJB Principles and Monitoring:** The initiative is guided by the 3Cs principle (Community, CSR, and Cost) to foster community ownership and develop cost-effective, local solutions. Progress is monitored via the online portal https://jsjb.mowr.gov.in.
* **JSA: CTR Evolution:** Jal Shakti Abhiyan was launched in 2019 in 256 water-stressed districts and relaunched as JSA: CTR in 2021 with the message "Catch the Rain: Where It Falls, When It Falls." Recent editions include JSA: CTR 2023 ("Source Sustainability for Drinking Water," 150 districts), JSA: CTR 2024 ("Nari Shakti se Jal Shakti," 151 districts), and JSA: CTR 2025 ("Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari: Jan Jagrukta Ki Or," 148 districts).
* **Regulatory and Supporting Frameworks:** The government promotes rainwater harvesting through MoJS guidelines (24.09.2020, amended 29.03.2023) for regulating groundwater extraction; MoHUA Model Building Bye-Laws (2016) mandating rainwater harvesting for buildings on plots of 100 sq. m. or more; CGWB's completion of NAQUIM for 25 lakh sq. km; and the Master Plan for Artificial Recharge to Groundwater-2020.
* **Complementary Schemes:** PMKSY-HKKP provides Central Assistance for Surface Minor Irrigation (SMI) and Repair, Renovation and Restoration (RRR) of Water Bodies. Expenditure on water-related works under MGNREGS is also tracked (details in Annexure-III).
